source_review.notes: Checked all seven cited standards and primary guidance sources. WHATWG HTML supports the event-stream grammar, EventSource reconnection, event/id/data/retry fields, comments, UTF-8, and Last-Event-ID behavior. RFC 6455 and RFC 8441 support WebSocket handshake, masking, control frames, Origin/security considerations, and HTTP/2 extended CONNECT. RFC 9421 supports covered-component signatures, key identifiers, creation/expiry/nonce parameters, and replay analysis. The CloudEvents HTTP Web Hooks profile and Standard Webhooks specification support HTTP delivery/response, endpoint-control, stable identifiers, timestamped signatures, rotation, exact-body verification, and idempotency patterns; the chapter identifies profile status rather than claiming a universal webhook standard. OWASP API7:2023 supports treating registered callback URLs as an SSRF boundary.

evidence: Checked immutable event e, attempts a_i, inbox I, delivery state D, retry schedule t_n, retained SSE sequence L_s, checkpoint c, queue Q(t), queue bound Q_max, and attempt count for consistent meaning.
Confirmed set membership/update, inequality, sequence interval, and at-least-once notation match the surrounding prose.
Confirmed acknowledgement, replay, resume, ordering, backpressure, liveness, and transport/application responsibility are defined separately.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Notation models safety boundaries without implying that transport receipt equals durable acceptance or business completion.

evidence: Confirmed Q(t) <= Q_max is a bound assertion rather than a measured performance claim and requires an explicit overflow action at equality.
Confirmed attempts(e) >= 1 describes successful at-least-once delivery while allowing duplicates and bounded retry.
Checked that ten worked examples and five exercise-answer pairs are present and sequentially numbered.
numerical_recomputation.notes: The chapter contains no workload-derived thresholds or benchmark claims; all operational values remain deployment-specific.

evidence: Constructed the lost-response trace: durable receiver accept followed by response loss and identical retry, proving stable ID plus atomic inbox prevents duplicate effect.
Constructed slow-consumer traces showing an open connection cannot bound memory unless enqueue is paired with pause, coalescing, shedding, disconnect, or external persistence.
Constructed reconnect traces showing TCP/WebSocket ordering on one connection cannot imply retained application replay across a new connection.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: The symbolic arguments distinguish safety, liveness, delivery, processing, and recovery claims.

evidence: Reviewed duplicate, delayed, reordered, expired, malformed, oversized, cross-tenant, unauthorized, and schema-incompatible webhook events plus timeout-after-commit and retry exhaustion.
Reviewed webhook registration redirects, DNS rebinding, private/link-local/metadata destinations, credentials, timestamp windows, nonce reuse, key rotation, disablement, dead-letter, and redrive.

Reviewed SSE fragmentation, multiline data, blank-line dispatch, buffering, retention gaps, forged Last-Event-ID, revocation, slow readers, and reconnect herds; reviewed WebSocket Origin/subprotocol, masking/UTF-8, compression bombs, floods, queue saturation, credential expiry, failover, resume forgery, and drain.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Coverage includes protocol edges, adversarial input, infrastructure intermediaries, lifecycle changes, and recovery ambiguity.

evidence: Confirmed webhook retries preserve event identity and governed signed content while attempt metadata changes separately.
Confirmed receiver acknowledgement follows an atomic inbox-and-accepted-work transition and duplicate paths do not repeat effects.
Confirmed SSE resume validates scope, current authorization, retained position, and reset behavior rather than trusting Last-Event-ID.
Confirmed WebSocket messages use explicit application IDs/acks/sequences and every transport has bounded messages, rates, queues, replay, connection lifetime, and slow-consumer behavior.
invariant_checking.notes: The invariants require durable stores and fault injection for deployment proof; protocol documentation alone is insufficient.

evidence: Reviewed the retry trace and confirmed response loss after commit refutes exactly-once transport while inbox deduplication preserves effect uniqueness within retention/atomicity assumptions.
Reviewed queue growth argument and confirmed finite Q_max requires explicit admission or overflow behavior under producer rate greater than consumer rate.
Reviewed reconnection argument and confirmed neither SSE event IDs nor WebSocket framing prove availability of an expired or unauthorized history.
Reviewed disconnect ambiguity and confirmed a recovery query/idempotent command ID is required when commit and acknowledgement can be separated by failure.
proof_review.notes: Arguments state their persistence, retention, authorization, and atomicity assumptions and avoid universal delivery claims.

evidence: Confirmed standards-defined wire behavior is separated from recommended application protocol and operations policy.
Confirmed CloudEvents HTTP Web Hooks is described as a named profile and Standard Webhooks as a usable specification, not as universal webhook semantics.
Confirmed at-least-once, durable acceptance, business completion, liveness, application acknowledgement, resume, and exactly-once effect are not conflated.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: Normative protocol facts, implementation patterns, local policy, and proof obligations remain distinguishable.

evidence: All seven references were retrieved and reviewed on 2026-09-02.
No latency, throughput, retention, retry-count, queue-size, or availability number is presented as an empirical universal.

Actual proxy buffering, signature interoperability, SSRF controls, replay stores, queue bounds, drain behavior, reconnect load, and recovery objectives remain explicit integration/load/chaos evidence obligations.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: No production webhook sender, browser/proxy path, WebSocket fleet, or broker was empirically assessed.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed channel selection, event identity, acknowledgement boundaries, sender/receiver state, signatures and replay, SSRF-safe registration, SSE grammar/resume, WebSocket subprotocol/resume, bounds, authorization, topology, draining, observability, and recovery as one consistent model.

practitioner_review.notes: Checked implementability through durable outbox/inbox records, leased attempts, classified jittered retry, key rotation, endpoint-control challenge, egress policy, retained authorized SSE logs, snapshot reset, versioned WebSocket envelopes, explicit acks, queue/rate/lifetime limits, drain signals, reconciliation, and fault/adversarial tests.

pedagogical_review.notes: The module first selects by interaction semantics, then develops webhook, SSE, and WebSocket mechanisms independently before comparing alternatives and composing operations. Ten examples isolate distinct failure windows; five exercises progress from guarantee classification and retry design to complete multi-channel architecture, with corresponding answers.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external academic or practitioner review is claimed.
